watchOS 27 is set to launch this fall as the next major software update for Apple Watch, introducing a handy new feature that can extend your Apple Watch battery life: "Proactive Battery Extension Notifications".

watchOS 27 can proactively extend your Apple Watch battery life by disabling features you never use.

watchOS 27 is coming soon and will bring two brand-new apps, a useful tap gesture, a new default Home Screen layout, three health-related upgrades, and more to Apple Watch.

Another new feature in watchOS 27 is designed to improve your Apple Watch battery life.

"Proactive Battery Extension Notifications" are a new type of alert you may see on your Apple Watch.

When you receive a battery extension notification, it means watchOS 27 has detected that you have several features you never use, and disabling them can save battery life.

These features include hand gestures, the "Raise to Speak" function used to summon Siri, and the "Start Workout" reminder, among others.

Each of the above features requires background processing to operate, which takes a toll on battery life.

Therefore, in watchOS 27, if the system detects that you have never used these features, it will automatically disable them. A "battery extension notification" will then be sent to inform you of the change and give you the option to keep them enabled.

If you do regularly use these features, you will never see this notification. Of course, you can also manually disable them yourself in Settings at any time to get longer battery life.

Apple has not specified exactly how much extra battery life users can gain from disabling these features. But it's obvious that the power savings are significant enough for Apple to develop this brand-new battery extension feature.

Do you usually use features like "Raise to Speak," hand gestures, or the "Start Workout" reminder on your Apple Watch? Will you keep them enabled afterward? Feel free to share with us in the comments.
